maximum was 20 connections per pod, and slow payment authorizations kept every
connection busy.

text:

title: ledger-config.txt
text:
Ledger consumer configuration notes (platform team)

ledger.retry_backoff_ms controls the initial delay between ledger write retries. The default is 250
and the delay doubles on each attempt up to ledger.max_attempts, which defaults to 8.

ledger.batch_size controls how many ledger entries are written per transaction. The default is 100.
Raising it above 500 has caused lock contention during month-end close and is not recommended.

Changes to these settings are made in config/ledger.properties and require a restart of the ledger
consumer. They are reviewed by the payments team.

text:

heading_path: Page 2
text:

title: Incident 2025-031 Postmortem: Checkout outage
heading_path: Page 1
text:
Incident 2025-031 Postmortem: Checkout outage
Summary: On 14 March 2025 checkout was unavailable for 47 minutes. Customers saw
HTTP 503 errors when placing orders. The incident was classified SEV1.
Root cause: orders-svc v3.8.1 exhausted its database connection pool after a
change that held connections open while calling the payments service. The pool
maximum was 20 connections per pod, and slow payment authorizations kept every
connection busy.

title: Orders Service Deployment Runbook
heading_path: Orders Service Deployment Runbook > Rolling deployment
text:
Deployments use a rolling strategy with a maximum of 25% of pods unavailable. Start the rollout with
`hctl deploy orders-svc --version v3.8.2` (substitute the version). Watch the error rate dashboard for
ten minutes after the rollout finishes.

title: Incident 2025-031 Postmortem: Checkout outage
heading_path: Page 2
text:
Resolution and follow-up actions
The on-call engineer rolled back to v3.8.0, which restored checkout. The fix,
released in orders-svc v3.8.2, releases the connection before calling payments
and raises the pool maximum to 40 connections per pod.
Action items: add an alert on connection pool saturation above 80 percent;
add a load test for slow upstream dependencies; document pool sizing in the
deployment runbook.

title: ledger-config.txt
text:
Ledger consumer configuration notes (platform team)

ledger.retry_backoff_ms controls the initial delay between ledger write retries. The default is 250
and the delay doubles on each attempt up to ledger.max_attempts, which defaults to 8.

ledger.batch_size controls how many ledger entries are written per transaction. The default is 100.
Raising it above 500 has caused lock contention during month-end close and is not recommended.

Changes to these settings are made in config/ledger.properties and require a restart of the ledger
consumer. They are reviewed by the payments team.

heading_path: Payments Service Error Code Reference > ERR-PAY-4012: Card authorization timeout
text:
Returned when the upstream card processor does not answer within 8 seconds. The client may retry
once with the same idempotency key. If more than 2% of authorizations fail with ERR-PAY-4012 over
five minutes, page the payments on-call engineer and check the processor status page.

title: Payments Service Error Code Reference
heading_path: Payments Service Error Code Reference > ERR-PAY-4020: Duplicate idempotency key
text:
The request reused an idempotency key with a different payload. This is a client bug; do not retry.
Log the `request_id` and contact the integrating team.

title: Payments Service Error Code Reference
heading_path: Payments Service Error Code Reference > ERR-PAY-5001: Ledger write failed
text:
The payment was authorized but the ledger write failed. The ledger consumer retries automatically
using `ledger.retry_backoff_ms` (default 250 ms, doubling up to 8 attempts). Do not refund manually
until the reconciliation job has run, otherwise the customer may be refunded twice.
